clue.text: Hollands bottle, so to speak, provides this

definitions.text: Hollands bottle, so to speak, provides this

parts.words: Hollands bottle, so to speak, provides this
parts.note: Hollands is Dutch gin and bottle is slang for nerve, so the clue describes the boldness a drink of gin is said to give

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollands' is a gin from the Netherlands, and 'bottle' is British slang for nerve; the bottle of gin supplies drink-fuelled bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for false bravery that comes from alcohol, which a bottle of Hollands gin would supply.

clue.text: Popular protest supported by movement out of control

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A popular protest was backed by a movement that ran out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' places DEMO above TIC in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic means of the common people, so it is a synonym of popular in the sense of belonging to ordinary folk.

clue.text: As fast as a motorbike, or not?

parts.note: the word not, written upwards as it would be in a down light, reads TON going up

explanation.surface: Is that really as quick as a motorbike, or not?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, says to write the clue word 'not' upwards, which gives TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton-up is a speed of a hundred miles an hour, the mark of a fast motorcyclist in British slang.

clue.text: Where you might find Violet, for example, in her element

definitions.text: Where you might find Violet, for example

parts.note: taken as written
barium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A woman called Violet is in her element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violet' looks like a woman's name, but here it is the flower, a pressed specimen in a plant collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a collection of dried plant specimens, where a pressed flower such as a violet would be kept.

clue.text: Not the sort of ball used in matches here

definitions.text: Not the sort of ball used in matches here

parts.words: Not the sort of ball used in matches here
parts.note: a London cricket ground shares its name with the egg shape of a rugby ball, yet only round balls are played there

explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; rugby uses an egg-shaped ball, but cricket there uses a round one.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape word describes a rugby ball and also names a famous cricket ground in south London, where such a ball is never used.

clue.text: One or two girls employed in perfume making

definitions.meaning: a single girl's name, or two names joined, Rose and Mary
an aromatic herb whose oil goes into scents

explanation.surface: One or two young women work at a perfumery.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a girl's name, made of two other names, and a fragrant herb whose oil is used in scents.

clue.text: Land held by Afghan army

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the words Afghan army

explanation.surface: Territory is occupied by the Afghan army.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa, so it is a land.

clue.text: This is sheer child's play

parts.note: a nursery game of hiding the face and peering out, with sheer hinting at a see-through blouse of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 'sheer child's play' reads as 'very easy', but it means a game played purely by children; a sheer garment shares its name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the game of covering one's face and revealing it to amuse a baby, a pastime for small children.

clue.text: Title composer announced

indicators.note: said out loud, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: Handel was a German-born composer who worked in London

explanation.surface: A composer's title is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or title by which someone is known.

clue.text: Smaller prisons for islanders

parts.note: minor means lesser or smaller
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Islanders are kept in smaller jails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the can' is American and British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Minorca, a Spanish Balearic island, are inhabitants of an island.

clue.text: A time put back for TV series

indicators.note: the phrase is read from end to start

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A time slot is postponed for a television series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses AN ERA (from 'A time') to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arena is a long-running BBC arts documentary series.

clue.text: One could come to opera wearing that

definitions.text: One could come to opera wearing that

indicators.note: the word that is put on around the abbreviation, as clothing goes around a body

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work such as an opera

explanation.surface: Someone could turn up at the opera dressed in formal headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts the word 'that' around OP. The whole clue also describes formal headgear worn to an evening at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat is traditional formal evening wear, the sort worn to a night at the opera.

clue.text: Boarded emergency rescue vessel when in fix

indicators.note: the vessel is put inside the word for fix

parts.note: to embed is to fix firmly in place
Noah's ark saved its passengers from the flood

explanation.surface: Someone boarded an emergency rescue boat when in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' looks like a predicament, but it means to set firmly in place; Noah's vessel is the emergency rescue boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship, so having boarded is a synonym.

clue.text: Pawn captured by attractive girl in competitive game

indicators.note: the pawn is held inside the word for the girl

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive young woman
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A pawn is taken by a pretty girl during a competitive match.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a match in a knockout football tournament, a fixture played to win.

clue.text: In drink after drink, bishop gets easily carried away

indicators.note: the first drink with its bishop comes behind the second

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: the bishop goes inside the first drink

parts.note: ale is beer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Drinking after drinking, a bishop gets easily swept off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried away' looks like excited, but with 'easily' it simply means light to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means light enough to be moved or taken along with ease.

clue.text: Play in extremely hard test

definitions.meaning: Arthur Miller's drama about the Salem witch trials

explanation.surface: A drama has a role in a very hard examination.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible is Miller's stage drama, and a crucible is also a searching ordeal.

clue.text: Fruit provided by schoolmate of Bunter. William

definitions.text: Fruit provided by schoolmate of Bunter. William

parts.words: Fruit provided by schoolmate of Bunter. William
parts.note: Billy Bunter's Greyfriars classmate is Bob Cherry; written surname first, as the clue writes 'Bunter, William', his name becomes a fruit term

explanation.surface: Fruit is supplied by a classmate of William Bunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Frank Richards' Greyfriars tales; his chum Bob Cherry, written surname first like Bunter's own name in the clue, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry bob is a pair of cherries on joined stalks, and, read register-style, also the name of Bunter's classmate.

clue.text: Tower of London's recent development

definitions.meaning: a fortified gate tower guarding a castle entrance
the City estate and arts centre built in the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: The Tower of London has a recent development.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbican is a defensive outwork with a tower, and the Barbican is a modern London housing and arts complex.

clue.text: In France. I admire cooked grouse

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: the letters of the word are mixed up as if cooked

explanation.surface: In France, I admire a cooked game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the bird to be cooked, but it means a complaint; 'cooked' rearranges ADMIRE into REMIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long lament or complaint, and to grouse is to grumble.

clue.text: Suitable name for male new arrival?

parts.note: just means fitting or deserved
in means arrived, as when a train is in

explanation.surface: A fitting name for a newborn boy?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer says newly arrived, which suits a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Fit, so live many years

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
long means for a great while

explanation.surface: Be healthy, and so live for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' seems to mean healthy, but it means to sit well among others.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to fit in or have a proper place somewhere.

clue.text: Cautious working of a drudge

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A drudge works carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarded means careful and wary, reluctant to commit oneself.

clue.text: Tolerates extra sound, but remains on the alert

parts.note: stands means puts up with

indicators.note: a word that is heard the same is entered in its place

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with extra noise but stays watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like noise, but it signals that BYE (a cricket extra, a run scored without the bat) is replaced by BY, said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by is to wait ready for action, staying alert.

clue.text: Man of action grabs wicket — it's natural talent

indicators.note: the man of action holds the wicket inside

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts rather than talks
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A man of action takes a wicket, showing innate ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Dower here means an endowment or natural gift, a talent one is born with.

clue.text: Offence given by article in war zone

parts.note: a crime is an offence
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An offence was reported by a newspaper article in a combat area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a news story, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea saw the 1850s war against Russia and later fighting, so it is a theatre of conflict.

clue.text: Girl raised capital after ruin

indicators.note: the raised piece follows the word for ruin

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: in a down light the letters are read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, like capital as an exclamation of approval

explanation.surface: A girl brought up capital after financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is the old word for excellent, A1 (read as AI); 'raised' turns it to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Invent something of value

definitions.meaning: to make up a new word or phrase

explanation.definitionFit: To coin a phrase is to make it up, and a coin is a piece of metal money.

clue.text: Relative gain after union negotiation

parts.note: a family member acquired through marriage, union here meaning a wedding rather than a trade body

explanation.walkthrough: 'union negotiation' suggests trade-union pay talks, but the union is a marriage, which brings new relations by law.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent, is acquired when two people wed.

clue.text: Dress editor severely criticized

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes

explanation.surface: A dress editor was harshly criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a noun for a frock, but CLOBBER is British slang for one's clothes and gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clobbered is to be hit hard, figuratively savaged by critics.

clue.text: Shackling committee that's involved in pressing business

parts.note: ironing means putting in irons or fetters
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A shackling committee deals with urgent matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing business' sounds urgent, but it is pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the padded stand on which clothes are pressed flat with an iron.
